insights.title: GST Annual Return: Checklist for FY 2024-25
insights.summary: Key points to review before filing your GST annual return and reconciliation.
body: The GST annual return (GSTR-9) and annual reconciliation (GSTR-9C where turnover exceeds the threshold) are important compliances for every registered person. Before filing, reconcile your books with returns filed during the year: GSTR-1, GSTR-3B, and e-invoice or e-way bill data where applicable.

Reconcile outward supplies with GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B. Match input tax credit (ITC) with GSTR-2B and your purchase register. Identify discrepancies early. Correct them through amendments or explain them in the annual return. Keep supporting documents ready for audit or notice.
Due dates are often extended by the GST Council. Check the latest notifications. Late fees and interest apply for delayed filing. For reconciliation or representation, contact your CA or our team.

insights.title: Tax Saving Options for Salaried Individuals
insights.summary: Section 80C, 80D, HRA, and other deductions to use before 31 March.
body: Salaried individuals can lower tax outgo through valid deductions and exemptions. Section 80C allows a deduction of up to ₹1.5 lakh for PPF, ELSS, EPF, life insurance premium, NSC, tuition fees, and housing loan principal repayment. Plan investments before 31 March to claim the benefit for the current financial year.

Section 80D covers health insurance premium (self, family, parents): up to ₹25,000, or ₹50,000 for senior citizens. HRA exemption depends on salary structure, rent paid, and city of residence. Also review Leave Travel Allowance (LTA), housing loan interest (Section 24), and whether the old or new tax regime suits you better.
A short review with your CA helps avoid missed claims. Arrange investments and documents (rent receipts, insurance premium proof, and similar) well before the deadline.

insights.title: MCA Compliance Calendar: Key Due Dates
insights.summary: ROC filings, AOC-4, MGT-7, and other company law compliances at a glance.
body: Companies and LLPs must meet several MCA and ROC due dates through the year. Key annual compliances include financial statements (AOC-4 for companies) and annual return (MGT-7), typically within 30 days and 60 days respectively from the conclusion of the AGM. For LLPs, Form 8 (Statement of Account) and Form 11 (Annual Return) have separate deadlines.

Event based filings cover changes in directors, registered office, capital, and charges. ADT-1 (auditor appointment), MGT-14 (for certain resolutions), and DIR-3 KYC for directors are also part of the calendar. Missing dates can lead to additional fees and disqualification risk.

Maintain an internal compliance calendar or work with your secretarial team or CA so nothing is missed. We support clients with ROC filings and compliance tracking across Varanasi, Delhi, Kolkata, and Bokaro.

insights.title: Startup India: Benefits and Registration
insights.summary: Eligibility, tax benefits, and how to register under the Startup India scheme.
body: Startup India supports innovation and growth through tax benefits, lighter compliance, and access to schemes. Eligibility generally requires incorporation as a private limited company, LLP, or partnership; turnover not exceeding ₹100 crore; and recognition as an eligible startup (typically within 10 years from incorporation).

Benefits include income tax exemption for three consecutive years in a block of seven years (subject to conditions), relaxation in compliance under the Companies Act, and faster patent processing. Registration is on the Startup India portal with supporting documents and a recommendation or recognition certificate.
We help startups with incorporation, DPIIT recognition, and ongoing compliance so they can build the business while staying eligible for benefits.

insights.title: TDS Compliance for Businesses: What to Track
insights.summary: Deduction, deposit, and return filing: a short guide to staying TDS compliant.
body: Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) applies to many payments: salary, rent, professional fees, contracts, interest, and more. As a deductor, deduct tax at the prescribed rates, deposit it by the due dates (usually the 7th of the following month), and file TDS returns (Q1 to Q4) in Form 24Q, 26Q, 27Q, and related forms.
Late deduction or deposit attracts interest and penalties. Issue TDS certificates (Form 16, 16A) to deductees on time. Use the TRACES portal for statements, corrections, and compliance status.
We help businesses set up TDS processes, reconcile TDS with books, and file returns so deductors and deductees stay compliant.

insights.title: Internal Audit: Best Practices for Mid-Size Firms
insights.summary: How to run an internal audit function that strengthens controls and processes.
body: Internal audit should strengthen controls, flag risks, and improve processes. For mid size companies, a risk based plan aligned with business objectives works well. Focus on high impact areas: revenue cycle, procurement, payroll, IT controls, and regulatory compliance.
Documentation, independence, and clear reporting to the audit committee or management matter. Use sampling and data analytics where practical. Follow up on prior findings until they are closed.
We provide internal audit services suited to your size and sector, with practical recommendations and follow through.

insights.title: GST Refunds: How to Claim and What to Expect
insights.summary: Eligibility, documentation, and timelines for export and inverted duty refunds.
body: GST refunds can arise from exports (zero rated supplies), inverted duty structure, or other specified cases. File the refund application on the portal (RFD-01 or through the return), upload supporting documents, and respond to deficiency memos or notices.

Export refunds usually need shipping bills, tax payment documents, and bank realisation proof. Inverted duty refunds need a statement of inward and outward supplies. Law prescribes timelines and interest on delayed refunds.
We assist with refund applications, reconciliation, and representation before authorities to secure refunds.

insights.title: Company Incorporation: A Practical Checklist
insights.summary: Documents, name approval, and post incorporation steps for new companies.
body: Incorporation involves name reservation (RUN or SPICe+), drafting MOA and AOA, obtaining DIN and DSC for directors, and filing the incorporation form. MCA SPICe+ combines name approval, incorporation, and several other applications (PAN, TAN, EPFO, ESIC) in one filing.

After incorporation, open a bank account, hold the first board meeting, and comply with ongoing ROC and tax filings. Keep identity and address proofs of directors and subscribers ready. Confirm the registered office address is valid.
We handle incorporation and post incorporation compliance so you can start operations without missing regulatory steps.

insights.title: Due Diligence for M&A: What Buyers and Sellers Should Know
insights.summary: Financial, tax, and legal checks that matter in mergers and acquisitions.
body: Due diligence helps buyers assess risk and value. It helps sellers prepare for a smoother transaction. Financial due diligence covers quality of earnings, working capital, debt, and contingent liabilities. Tax due diligence reviews past returns, pending assessments, and potential exposure.

Legal and compliance diligence covers contracts, litigation, IP, and regulatory approvals. Scope can be adjusted to deal size and risk. A disciplined process reduces surprises and supports negotiation and documentation.
We provide financial and tax due diligence for acquisitions, investments, and divestments, with clear reports and practical recommendations.

insights.title: Government Schemes for MSMEs: A Quick Overview
insights.summary: Central and state schemes MSMEs can use for support and incentives.
body: MSMEs can access many Central and State schemes: interest subsidies, capital investment support, quality certification, export promotion, and others. Udyam registration is often the first step. Eligibility and documentation vary by scheme.

Track new schemes and amendments. Many applications are online. Missing deadlines can mean losing benefits. We help MSMEs identify relevant schemes, prepare applications, and maintain compliance for continued eligibility.
Contact us to discuss which schemes fit your business and how we can support the process.
